orbits.scope: Circular eclipsing-binary orbit; period and inclination adopted from Torres & Ribas 2002. The fitted HJD0=2449345.116643 +/- 0.000068 is an eclipse reference, not a periastron epoch. Node, argument and periastron remain unavailable rather than fabricating sky geometry.

axisSource.scope: Published relative axis from the adopted cluster distance, not rescaled with the legacy catalog parallax. The cluster-distance assumption is explicit in Table 4.

orbits.scope: GRAVITY+AMBER relative stellar orbit; omega is published for the WR component (MSC Aa). The app projects secondary Ab relative to primary Aa with the required 180-degree argument conversion. No wide A-B or A-C orbit is inferred. The source reports omega_WR=67.5 and node-line PA Omega=247 degrees. For the app convention (secondary O relative to primary WR, with primary omega converted by 180 degrees), the equivalent projection node is 67 degrees. This normalization reproduces the signed RA/Dec offsets of Table 1; using 247 directly would reverse both stars. Preserve the reported node and argument for display.

orientationDerivation.scope: The source reports omega_WR=67.5 and node-line PA Omega=247 degrees. For the app convention (secondary O relative to primary WR, with primary omega converted by 180 degrees), the equivalent projection node is 67 degrees. This normalization reproduces the signed RA/Dec offsets of Table 1; using 247 directly would reverse both stars. Preserve the reported node and argument for display.
orientationDerivation.validation: GRAVITY/VLTI offsets in Table 1, including 2023-11-13: WR relative to O at RA=-2.26 mas, Dec=-1.58 mas.

orbits.scope: Confirmed close spectroscopic binary with explicitly normalized Aa/Ab labels. The source publishes an argument of periastron of 255.6 +/- 12.2 degrees, but no astrometric node. Leave the rendered sky orientation unavailable; do not invent a node or ambiguous argument convention.

Relative Ab-to-Aa interferometric orbit. All published intervals are 2.3-97.7 percentiles, approximately two sigma; an alternative node/argument plus 180 degrees is allowed. Physical axis uses the publication distance, not the legacy component parallax.

axisSource.scope: Published adopted distance and error are at two sigma.

totalDynamicalMass.scope: Total Aa+Ab mass, with two-sigma bounds; never an individual component mass.

Preserve the publication distance assumption; no individual constant orbital velocities are assigned.

axisSource.scope: Formal joint-solution MCMC distance; abstract/profile-likelihood distance is 24.30 +/- 0.05 pc.

epochSource.sourceConvention: Equation 5; combined fit dates are HJD minus 2400000, not MJD.

orbits.orientationValidation: Relative secondary offsets reproduce the signed Table 3 positions at MJD 60232.4493, 60234.5388 and 60259.3951 when observation times are converted to HJD. No 180-degree primary-argument conversion is applied to the published combined sky solution.
